races.name: Pinker's Pond Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Jenni
runners_data.note: Holds up for a late run and has place form on similar Going (12/15 sim-going runs), but trainer Seb Spencer is winless from 5 runs in the last 14 days and 51 days off the track adds an element of doubt about sharpness.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent sequence - unplaced last time and little impact in her last four - though a third five runs back hints at more, and our rating still puts her clear on merit. A long lay-off and 135lb to shoulder are queries, but she has already raced over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Saisons D'or
runners_data.note: Trainer Jedd O'Keeffe is in red-hot form at 4/4 over the last 14 days, which is the standout angle here; races as a hold-up type but has proven 7f form on Good ground and ran 1st last time out at this trip, making him dangerous from just off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Landed a race three starts back and rates competitive on figures, though a 7th last time and a 5th before that make the recent sequence look underwhelming. He's already proven over today's trip and going, and with 23 days since his last outing, capable of bouncing back close to that winning form under 135lb.

runners_data.name: Classy Clarets
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with excellent recent form — won over 7f on Good ground last time and placed in four of five career starts on similar going; headgear fitted, 8 days since last run and trainer Iain Jardine sends runners out fit, making this a live contender in the expected race shape.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and returns quickly, just 8 days later, from a yard in good form with 8 winners from its last 29 runners. A first-time hood could sharpen him further, and he already goes well over today's trip and going, though the modest speed figure is the one blot under 135lb.

runners_data.name: Filey Beach
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner whose style fit score (0.93) signals she will operate comfortably in her natural role leading from the front; three wins from 9 runs on Good-to-Firm type going at 7f underlines the suitability of conditions, though apprentice Taryn Langley (3lb) needs to ride her patiently enough to avoid setting too strong a pace.
runners_data.comment: Won twice in his last five starts and ran to a solid third last time, giving him claims on his best form, and he already goes well over today's trip and going. Working against him: a 36-day break since that run and a yard that's currently out of form, with just 1 winner from its last 31 runners.

runners_data.name: Groundsman
runners_data.note: Has shown only place form at 7f on Soft and Stamina ground with zero wins in similar-going conditions; the headgear flag (p) suggests he can be keen early which, in a race where midfield will be congested, represents a risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but has been a model of consistency, with two thirds among them, and our figures rate him second best of this field. First-time cheekpieces could be the added sharpener he needs, and he already goes well over today's trip and going under 134lb.

runners_data.name: Coconut Bay
runners_data.note: Genuinely races as a hold-up type but the field's composition has pushed him into a midfield slot he may not want; trainer Davidson is 3/9 over 14 days, which is a positive angle, but the style-fit discount (0.93) tempers expectations given his natural closing instincts are compromised by the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but ran a fair 4th last time and is out again quickly, just 8 days later. She already goes well over today's trip and going, though her figures leave her firmly in the pack rather than among the leading players under 129lb.

runners_data.name: Without Delay
runners_data.note: A true closer by nature whose best form over 7f on Good ground came from the back, yet the traffic-heavy midfield he is likely to find himself in here makes his task harder; trainer Waggott has no runners in form over 14 days and the horse is off a career-low OR of 47.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and only fitfully in the frame since a third a few runs back, she sits towards the bottom of this field on figures. In her favour, first-time cheekpieces and a lenient 122lb might sharpen her up, with just 8 days since her latest run keeping her fresh and ready.

runners_data.name: Indy's Angel
runners_data.note: Form figures of 878802 are unimpressive and the horse has failed to win in 15 similar-going appearances; naturally wants to come from the rear but the race map places him in midfield, and the style displacement (0.91) further dims prospects on what is a modest profile.
runners_data.comment: Hard to fancy overall for a winless sequence of mostly rear-of-field finishes, though a much-improved 2nd last time out is the one form line in her favour. First-time cheekpieces and a fair 121lb might help her find more, with just 7 days since that promising run.

runners_data.name: Summer Rain
runners_data.note: The weakest going-form profile in the race with only 4 comparable runs from 13 on similar ground and no wins or places in similar conditions; a genuine hold-up type operating out of position in midfield, and trainer Lidster's recent strike rate of 1/18 over 14 days does not add confidence.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of this field on our figures and hasn't threatened the frame in his last five starts, with a 9th last time doing him no favours. He does have experience of today's trip and is race-fit enough having run just 12 days ago, but there's little else in the profile to inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Filey Beach is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to press her, is expected to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over Catterick's 7f. The field is unusually hold-up heavy, but Coconut Bay, Without Delay, Indy's Angel and Summer Rain are all true closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Classy Clarets and Saisons D'or are the most likely to push forward and fill the prominent berths behind Filey Beach. With one uncontested leader controlling a modest tempo on fast ground, the race shape strongly favours horses able to sit close to the pace and travel comfortably — prominent racers and those capable of sitting just off the leader will have a decisive positional advantage over genuine hold-up horses who will face a wall of rivals and a potentially insufficient final-furlong surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Filey Beach Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Filey Beach meets no early pressure and dictates an uncontested, sustainable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Filey Beach sets her own fractions on Good to Firm ground and the prominent horses behind her race in a draught before a late challenge materialises; the steady pace suits those with tactical speed who can quicken off it. Classy Clarets, already proven at 7f on Good going and with recent form in excellent shape, and Saisons D'or, whose trainer is in hot form at 4/4 over 14 days, are best placed to pounce from close range.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Pressurise Early
scenarios.trigger: If Classy Clarets or Saisons D'or push forward and impose a contested pace on Filey Beach.
scenarios.body: Increased early fractions on the fast ground will stretch the field and make the race a test of stamina from halfway; runners who race prominently and stay well will have a clear edge over those needing a late sprint. Classy Clarets has the headgear, the class and the Catterick-friendly profile to repel challengers if the tempo is genuinely strong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and creates a genuine end-to-end gallop that opens the race up for closers.
scenarios.body: A fast true pace would compress the gaps in the closing stages and give a well-timed late run a chance, but the majority of hold-up horses here have been displaced from their natural position and may struggle to obtain the wide run they need on a track where the draw and pace count. Jenni has the best recent similar-going form record among the hold-up contingent and represents the best hope if the race falls apart at the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Traffic Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed pack of redistributed hold-up types causes interference, interfering with the normal race flow.
scenarios.body: With four genuine closers forced to race in midfield and competing for limited gaps, trouble in running becomes a real risk and the outcome could be decided by traffic luck as much as ability. Any horse with the pace to travel in the top three and avoid the midfield scrimmage would benefit, and Filey Beach could steal the race if the field ties itself in knots chasing her.

watchPoints.text: Classy Clarets has won and placed repeatedly at this trip on Good ground with headgear fitted — if Filey Beach's uncontested lead produces an attainable target, this runner is the primary threat to steal a prominent win.

The four redistributed hold-up types (Coconut Bay, Without Delay, Indy's Angel, Summer Rain) will all be competing for the same midfield space — watch for a scrimmage and potential interference between the 4f and 2f markers.
Saisons D'or's trainer form (4/4 in 14 days) is the sharpest angle in the race and could be underestimated if punters focus on the pace map rather than the form book — monitor market moves.

Filey Beach's apprentice rider Taryn Langley (3lb) has not ridden her before; if she sets too strong a pace trying to establish control, it could compress the winning margin and open the race to closers in SCENARIO_C.

Good to Firm conditions are confirmed across all Catterick races today — any horse with a Soft or Heavy going preference should be treated with significant scepticism, and Groundsman (best form on Soft) looks vulnerable in these conditions.

races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Nursery

runners_data.name: Bellatina
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Charlie Johnston who has placed twice at this trip on good ground — Connor Beasley's positional instincts in small fields are a plus and her form figures suggest she finds the line without winning, making the step up in tactical clarity here intriguing.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in her last four starts but a strong second last time hints she's building towards one, bookended by another runner-up effort four runs back. Already proven over today's trip and going, and quick to reappear just 13 days on, she rates a leading threat under 135lb, though the two moderate runs in between are the slight worry.

runners_data.name: Najmet Minzaal
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and unexposed after just two starts both on good or standard ground — Kevin Stott handles prominently-ridden types well and the absence of a win or place on the board yet is offset by the fact both runs were on potentially unsuitable surfaces for a quick-ground type.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced, with two solid 4ths in her last two starts and still without a win, though our figures like her on the clock with the best speed figure among these dangers. Quick to back up again just 11 days on and already proven over today's trip and going, but the unrewarded profile so far is the obvious slight query under 135lb.

runners_data.name: Penny Capri
runners_data.note: Consistent back-of-the-field finisher who hasn't troubled the judge in three attempts, but David Loughnane's horses sometimes need an extra run to find their feet and the headgear absence is notable; the faster conditions suit more than the soft she ran on last time.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last three starts but boasts the best figures of this field on both form and the clock, and a first-time hood could be exactly the source of encouragement she needs to translate that into a big run. Already proven over today's trip and going and fit again quickly, just 11 days on, she's the one to beat under 133lb, with the finishing positions so far the only blot.

runners_data.name: Mardy Bum
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up style held up in the rear by nature and returning after 34 days, with David O'Meara's yard in reasonable nick — three starts all on good or standard ground and a best effort of fourth suggests modest ceiling but consistent placement without a clean run through.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and rated towards the bottom of this field on both figures and the clock, a 34-day absence adding to the questions. A steadier 4th last time is a shred of form to cling to, and the first-time hood may bring a change worth watching, but she has plenty to find under 132lb.

runners_data.name: Lairy Mary
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner who has already won over this exact trip and course configuration, going good — Duran Fentiman's low-key booking is worth noting but on pace terms she inherits an uncontested lead and Tim Easterby's sprinters are reliable on fast ground.
runners_data.comment: Won two runs back but has since faded to a 6th last time out, and a 34-day gap since that run adds another question mark. She's already proven over today's trip and going and holds fair form claims from that win, but she's rated towards the back of this field and has plenty to prove under 130lb.

runners_data.name: Fortunate
runners_data.note: True hold-up type whose natural position at the rear is squeezed by the volume of similar horses in the race — Eve Johnson Houghton's juvenile has struggled for consistency with a best of fourth, and the honest 0.90 style-fit flag means this run may be contested from a position that doesn't suit.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but a fair 5th last time and a 4th before that show she's going the right way, and our figures place her among the leading dangers on both merit and the clock. First-time cheekpieces could sharpen her further, and she already has experience of today's distance, though a 31-day break is a mild concern under 130lb.

runners_data.name: Explainingislosing
runners_data.note: Has shown one piece of notable form (a third at 5f good) among otherwise moderate efforts — Oisin Orr is an upgrade in the saddle and Richard and Peter Fahey are capable of producing sharply-improved juveniles, though being a natural hold-up type squeezed into midfield by the field's shape complicates the task.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out and without a win in his last four starts, though our figures rate him well above his current mark and he backs that up with a solid figure on the clock. He does have experience of today's distance and looks workably weighted at 124lb, but the finishing positions so far leave plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Arcadian Days
runners_data.note: Jack Morland's runner has three runs all over 5f on good ground and hasn't beaten many horses home yet — Jason Hart is a reliable northern jockey but the trainer's 0/6 14-day record and the horse's redistribution away from its preferred deep hold-up slot are quiet negatives.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in her last three starts and yet to threaten the frame, though our figures rate her well clear of her current mark and she's already proven over today's trip and going. A 37-day absence is the obvious concern, but a workable 123lb may help her make more of an impression than the bare form suggests.

runners_data.name: Mr Darling
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field with figures of 6-6-10 and no form on going better than good — Bryan Smart's 1/13 in-form figure is modest and while Cam Hardie rides competently, the hold-up style mapped to midfield leaves this runner with minimal tactical edge.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of this field on our figures and without a win in his last three starts, with 6ths in his last two runs and an unplaced effort before that doing little to inspire. He is fresh enough having run just 18 days ago and does have experience of today's trip and going, but there's little in the profile to suggest he can trouble these.

races.paceDynamic: Lairy Mary is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 9-runner 5f nursery on Good to Firm ground at Catterick, and with no genuine challenger for the lead she will coast out of the gates and set whatever tempo suits her, likely a steady-to-moderate gallop that keeps her fresh into the final furlong. The remainder of the field — Bellatina, Najmet Minzaal, Penny Capri, Mardy Bum, Fortunate, Explainingislosing, Arcadian Days and Mr Darling — are all hold-up or prominent types by nature, yet the field holds more hold-up and prominent horses than the map can accommodate at the rear; Bellatina and Najmet Minzaal, with their proximity to pace in recent runs, are most likely to actually secure prominent positions, while Fortunate, Explainingislosing, Arcadian Days and Mr Darling are mapped to midfield despite being true hold-up types because they cannot all find space at the back. With Lairy Mary dictating an uncontested lead on quick ground over the minimum trip, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can travel smoothly in behind and produce a finish from the dip — those running closest to pace without burning energy early carry the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lairy Mary Dictates Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Lairy Mary jumps well and controls fractions with no meaningful pressure, turning a sprint into a controlled test.
scenarios.body: She sets a comfortable lead that keeps her fresh enough to maintain momentum through Catterick's short run-in, and with the field stretched behind her in a strung-out single file the horse best able to track her close and deliver a sustained finish benefits most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sits a length or two off Lairy Mary, bides time and quickens past inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Bellatina or Najmet Minzaal, racing just off the leader in a race with little genuine pace pressure, avoids the traffic issues likely to affect the back-of-field cluster and produces a clean run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lairy Mary Fades, Closer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early fractions prove faster than they appear and Lairy Mary ties up close home, creating a gap for a finisher.
scenarios.body: A genuinely held-up horse who has tracked midfield without spending energy — most likely Fortunate or Explainingislosing — gets through on the inside as the leader weakens, though the redistribution of these hold-up types into midfield means the position they actually race from may not be their true comfort zone.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Bunching Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large hold-up cluster fails to find clear runs in the final two furlongs and the race becomes messy with multiple horses checked.
scenarios.body: With four or more true hold-up types all seeking the same racing room simultaneously, interference and traffic problems can negate finishing pace and hand the race back to the front two or three on the premise that they never lost momentum.

watchPoints.text: Lairy Mary jumps from stall and is tracked — if any runner attempts to dispute the lead in the first furlong, watch for Lairy Mary's stride pattern shortening sooner than expected and the race blowing wide open.

Bellatina posted a placed effort just 13 days ago and Connor Beasley will be looking to travel close to Lairy Mary — if she secures that position at the first bend, she avoids the traffic that could engulf the hold-up cluster late.

Fortunate, Explainingislosing, Arcadian Days and Mr Darling are all genuine hold-up types packed into the same midfield zone — watch the run from two furlongs out for interference as all four seek the same gaps simultaneously.

Going is reported Good to Firm for this race despite the headline card stating Good — that extra quickness over 5f at Catterick will sharpen early splits and could catch the more lightly-raced Najmet Minzaal out if she has not encountered genuine fast ground before.

races.name: Racing TV Profits Returned To Racing Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
All Races Live On Racing TV Handicap

runners_data.name: Master Of Entropy
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse for Quinn, well beaten in six of his last seven starts, with no wins or placed efforts on similar going; Jason Hart will be looking for a pace scenario that simply hasn't materialised in this horse's recent runs.
runners_data.comment: Master Of Entropy is winless in his last five starts, though a third sits among them and he ran fourth last time. He has today's trip and ground covered and a fair speed figure, but sits near the bottom of these figures, making him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Starryfield
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, getting back into her natural role after a 62-day break; James Owen's yard has been very active (9 winners from 46 in 14 days) and Oisin Orr is a strong pairing, with the solo lead a clear tactical asset if she can control tempo unchallenged.
runners_data.comment: Starryfield has been remarkably consistent without getting his head in front, with two seconds and two thirds among his last five starts, including third again last time. He tops these figures clearly and returns fresh from a lengthy break, needing only to convert that form into a breakthrough.

runners_data.name: Indefensible
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing type for Ollie Pears who has placed in three of his last seven runs on good ground; Harry Russell takes the ride and the horse's ability to sit just off the pace in 7f is a genuine fit for this race shape, though the trainer's recent 14-day record (0/10) is modest.
runners_data.comment: Indefensible is winless in his last five starts but has twice finished runner-up in that time, form that ranks him third on these figures. He has today's trip and ground covered and returns having had a fair break, though his form has been up and down rather than progressive.

runners_data.name: Beyond The Bar
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good ground and has shown willingness to come from off the pace; David Allan provides a stable jockey booking for Easterby, but the consistent distance of 8f+ in his form makes 7f a query, and he has finished 5th, 7th, 7th in his three most recent outings.
runners_data.comment: Beyond The Bar won five starts back but form dipped through a run of sevenths, before he nudged back to fifth last time. He has today's trip and ground covered and sits second on these figures, so there are signs he could be rounding back into form.

runners_data.name: Masaban
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes over on this Edward Bethell-trained prominent runner who won over 8f on good ground and placed over the same trip on soft; the drop back to 7f and step onto faster ground is a slight unknown, but the prominent style fits this race shape well, making him one of the most interesting profile fits on the card.
runners_data.comment: Masaban won three starts back and has stayed competitive since, following that success with a third and a fifth last time. He has today's trip and ground covered and ranks among the leading group on these figures, though his placings have drifted gently since that win.

runners_data.name: Magistery
runners_data.note: Has been running in softer conditions throughout his career (four of five runs on soft) and this good-to-firm surface at Catterick is a significant step up in ground firmness; Connor Beasley partners a horse who is a natural hold-up type finishing off the pace, which is the profile facing the hardest task in today's shape.
runners_data.comment: Magistery won four starts back but has since tailed off, following a fifth with back-to-back unplaced efforts, the latest last time out. She has today's trip and ground covered, but that decline and a 48-day gap make her hard to fancy down these figures.

runners_data.name: Dacres Cross
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott partners a Kevin Ryan-trained prominent type whose form figures of 4,11,6,7,17 on good ground are deeply uninspiring; nine from ten sim-going runs outside the frame suggests fast conditions are a recurring concern, and prominent tactics may not be enough to compensate.
runners_data.comment: Dacres Cross is winless in his last five starts but did find some improved form to finish fourth last time out. Today's trip and ground are covered, though a 46-day break and a modest recent record leave obvious questions for a midfield contender on these figures.

runners_data.name: Harswell Angel
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's filly has run five consecutive 4th-or-worse finishes, all at 7f on good ground; her true running style is that of a hold-up horse pushed to the rear of the field, sitting behind the redistributed midfield group rather than in it as mapped — Joanna Mason will need a very different race shape to get her involved.
runners_data.comment: Harswell Angel is winless in his last five starts, with three straight eighths before an improved fifth last time out. He has today's trip and ground covered and a fair speed figure, though the run of below-par efforts makes him tricky to fully trust.

runners_data.name: Bye Law
runners_data.note: Running for a notably in-form Easterby yard (15 from 104 in 14 days) and carrying a hood, Bye Law showed back-to-back 3rds on good ground earlier in his form but has regressed since; his natural position is at the back of the field and being mapped forward is cosmetic — in reality he will likely race deep and face the same late-surge challenge as the other held-up types.
runners_data.comment: Bye Law is winless in his last six starts but had shown ground with back-to-back thirds before his most recent unplaced effort. First-time cheekpieces and a quick 11-day turnaround could help him bounce back, and he has today's trip and ground covered despite that dip last time.

runners_data.name: Vega Storm
runners_data.note: Fahey's 3yo has placed in three of four career starts but all on softer surfaces (SOF/STA), and this represents the firmest ground he has encountered; a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, he will be racing from the rear despite the midfield mapping, and Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim may not be enough to offset the style and ground concerns.
runners_data.comment: Vega Storm is winless in his last four starts and his form has faded, following back-to-back thirds with a fifth and an unplaced effort last time. A fair speed figure is his one asset, but sitting bottom of these figures on a downward curve makes him hard to support.

races.paceDynamic: Starryfield is the one confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine rival likely to press hard from the off on good-to-firm ground at Catterick's 7f, she should be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a true searching pace. Masaban, Indefensible and Dacres Cross are the prominent types who will contest the early positions behind her, creating a race run at honest but not punishing fractions — the kind of tempo that keeps hold-up horses in arrears rather than delivering a late swoop. Harswell Angel, Bye Law and Vega Storm are genuine off-the-pace types who are mapped into midfield positions purely because there is nowhere else to put them; in reality they will likely be tracking the field from the rear and facing a significantly tougher task than their map position implies, making a late surge harder to land. This shape — a controlled pace, a solo front-runner, prominent horses in a strong tactical position — strongly favours runners who can sit just off Starryfield's shoulder and pounce from a prominent berth in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Starryfield Controls, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Starryfield gets a clean lead at a sustainable gallop and prominent rivals track without interference.
scenarios.body: Starryfield bowls along uncontested, setting a gallop that keeps hold-up horses from landing a meaningful blow; the prominent duo of Masaban and Indefensible, sitting second and third, are best placed to collar her in the Catterick straight when the injection of pace comes.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves even steadier than expected and Starryfield quickens away from a crawl in the straight.
scenarios.body: A slowly-run 7f at Catterick can turn into a sprint finish, but if the field holds tight and Starryfield times her kick to perfection, she can prove hard to catch; her STYLE_FIT flag means racing in role here is a genuine asset and Oisin Orr's judgement of pace becomes decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Injected, Hold-Ups Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If a rival tests Starryfield early and the fractions increase significantly, stringing out the field.
scenarios.body: A genuinely faster gallop would compress the pack less, potentially opening a lane for hold-up horses to motor through late; Master Of Entropy and Beyond The Bar are the two natural off-the-pace runners with the best going form for these conditions, giving them the best chance if the scenario materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If traffic issues disrupt the prominent horses late and a midfield drifter emerges from the pack.
scenarios.body: Redistribution of Harswell Angel, Bye Law and Vega Storm into the same midfield band as natural prominents creates congestion risk on Catterick's turning straight; if the race breaks up unexpectedly, a horse like Beyond The Bar or Magistery, racing from a genuine off-the-pace position, could benefit from others checking.

watchPoints.text: Masaban — Daniel Tudhope on a horse whose prominent style is a perfect fit for a Starryfield-led tempo; watch whether he travels comfortably just off the pace into the straight, as that position will be decisive.

Harswell Angel, Bye Law and Vega Storm — all three are true hold-up types compressed into a midfield map position; if they settle deep as their natural style dictates, the sustainable pace set by Starryfield leaves them with too much ground to make up.

Dacres Cross — Kevin Ryan's runner has consistently failed on good ground across nine sim-going runs with only one placed effort; watch whether the market shortens or drifts in the ring as a guide to stable confidence.

Starryfield — 62 days off the track is notable; watch her in the paddock and market moves for any sign the layoff has sharpened or dulled her, as her ability to stride on uncontested is the single biggest determinant of race shape.
Magistery — four of five career runs on soft or heavy; if the going dries further toward firm, watch for him to be an early market drifter as his form profile is entirely ground-dependent.

races.name: Bet At racingtv.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Not So Sobers
runners_data.note: Three wins from six runs at 2m on Good ground make this the standout staying profile in the race; David Killahena & Graeme McPherson send him out in fair nick (T14: 3/9) and Daniel Tudhope provides a strong jockey booking, with 39 days since last run representing a typical prep gap for this horse.
runners_data.comment: Not So Sobers arrives full of confidence having won last time out and clearly retains ability on this evidence. Today's trip and ground are covered and a first-time hood is fitted, with only the mixed efforts further back a note of caution against following that upturn blindly.

runners_data.name: Bunker Bay
runners_data.note: A 180-day absence is the obvious concern, but Micky Hammond has a 1/7 strike rate in the last 14 days suggesting horses are fit, and this mare's two wins at 2m on Good ground give her the correct profile; tongue-piece headgear applied, and her two recent victories over today's trip underline the distance suitability.
runners_data.comment: Bunker Bay tops these figures and owns a leading speed figure, with a second among his last five starts the standout effort. He has experience at today's trip and wears first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces today, so turning those placed efforts into a breakthrough is the obvious next step.

runners_data.name: Himself
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse in terms of natural style, though the map places him in midfield due to the cluster of closers — his form shows one win from 14 runs at 14f on Standard, and his recent Good-ground record (5th, 6th) over shorter trips is unconvincing at today's distance; Style Fit of 0.92 tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Himself opened this sequence with back-to-back wins but has since cooled, without adding to that tally across his last four starts. Today's trip and ground are covered and a fair speed figure keeps him involved, though he needs to rediscover that early spark to feature again at the finish.

runners_data.name: Speechman
runners_data.note: A five-day turnaround is very quick, and the fade-in-finish flag is a direct red light for a 2m contest — Speechman's best going form is moderate (4/15 on similar ground, 0 wins) and he has been out of the first three in his last four starts; hood headgear and a low OR of 49 are minor compensations, but his natural style is a hold-up type squeezed into midfield on the map.
runners_data.comment: Speechman is winless in his last five starts but has been building nicely, improving to third last time out just five days ago. First-time visor and a fair speed figure add encouragement, though he still needs to convert that upward curve into a big result.

runners_data.name: Lady Buttercup
runners_data.note: Donald McCain sends her out 58 days fresh with a tongue-tie applied, and while she has one placing at 2m on Good, her last five runs show no wins and she has been troubled by trips shorter than today's; her redistribution out of the rear reflects a true hold-up style, and an OR of 48 is rock bottom in this field.
runners_data.comment: Lady Buttercup is winless in her last four starts and the trend has softened, a fifth and fourth giving way to a seventh and an unplaced effort latest. She has experience of today's going and a fair speed figure, but a 58-day absence adds to the doubts and she sits low on these figures.

runners_data.name: Sugarpiehoneybunch
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has done most of his recent racing on Soft ground (four of last five on Soft), today's Good to Firm is a notable going concern; Rhys Elliott (5lb claim) is an asset in theory, but Simon West has a minimal two-run yard form in 14 days, and a sequence of 7th-8th finishes on Good ground gives little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Sugarpiehoneybunch is winless in her last five starts and has struggled to threaten the frame, a fifth at the start of this spell the best of a run of sevenths and an eighth. She has today's trip and ground covered, but sits bottom of these figures and is hard to recommend.

races.paceDynamic: With all six runners carrying hold-up profiles and no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 2m Catterick contest on Good to Firm ground is likely to crawl into life before developing into a tactical, stamina-sapping finish. The pace dynamic note flags that Himself, Speechman, Lady Buttercup, and Sugarpiehoneybunch are all true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map — none of these four are likely to establish early position, meaning the race tempo will be shaped by whoever blinks first and pushes forward from a reluctant field. Not So Sobers and Bunker Bay, both with winning form at 2m+ on Good ground and the most credible staying profiles in the race, are best equipped to benefit from a slowly-run, late-kicking contest. This race shape strongly favours the classiest, most proven stayer who can travel comfortably in a dawdling gallop and produce a sustained finish — Not So Sobers and Bunker Bay hold the edge in that profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dawdle Into Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field idles through the early stages and the race turns into a 3f dash from home on quick ground.
scenarios.body: With no true front-runner, the tempo will be artificially slow, compressing the field and turning Catterick's 2m into a test of speed over the final quarter-mile rather than stamina. Not So Sobers, a winner twice over this trip on Good, and Bunker Bay, proven at 2m+ on similar ground, are best placed to handle the quick finish having travelled well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Develops
scenarios.trigger: If one runner pushes forward early, setting a genuine gallop that strings the field out over the last mile.
scenarios.body: A real pace on Good to Firm at 2m sorts out the stayers from the passengers, and only horses with genuine staying form survive; Not So Sobers has won over 2m on Good and Bunker Bay has a strong record at 2m+ including two recent wins. Speechman and Lady Buttercup, who have struggled beyond a mile and a half in soft form, are likely to get outpaced when the race becomes a true test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed hold-up runner happens to be produced late with a perfectly timed run in a race that fractures at the 3f pole.
scenarios.body: Himself ran well on his latest start over 14f on Good and carries a light weight, giving him a marginal chance if the race develops a genuine end-to-end gallop that suits a late finisher — though his redistribution tag and Style Fit of 0.92 tempers confidence. Lady Buttercup has one placing at 2m and rides off a low mark with Andrew Mullen, but her recent form is modest and her short-trip history limits optimism.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals Race
scenarios.trigger: If one runner breaks clear unchallenged from the start and dictates such a slow early pace that they steal a decisive lead before the field wakes up.
scenarios.body: In a field void of a natural front-runner, a jockey who decides to take matters into their own hands could exploit the vacuum and build an unassailable advantage, particularly on fast ground where a bold front-running display is hardest to reel in. Speechman, despite a fade-in-finish flag, or Sugarpiehoneybunch could theoretically steal this role, though both are genuine hold-up types whose chance under this scenario should be heavily discounted.

watchPoints.text: Not So Sobers and Bunker Bay dominate the staying profile — watch whether either is positioned early enough to control the tactical pace, as in a slow-run race the winner is likely to come from this pair.

Speechman ran just five days ago and carries a fade-in-finish flag over 2m — watch for early signs of laboured movement or reluctance entering the final turn, which would confirm him as a non-runner in the finish.

Bunker Bay's 180-day absence is a significant fitness query despite the trainer's recent form — watch her in the paddock and opening furlong for any sign of ring-rustiness before taking her on at short odds.

With no natural front-runner in the field, watch whether any jockey decides to take up the running from the off — whoever leads on the first circuit controls the tempo and could exploit a field of reluctant closers.

Going is reported Good to Firm for this race specifically, faster than it reads on paper — watch which horses are best handling the surface in earlier races as Sugarpiehoneybunch's Soft-ground profile makes him particularly vulnerable to the underfoot conditions.

races.name: Racing Again 15th July Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Donna Nook
runners_data.note: O'Meara and Tudhope is a strong combination at this level; suited by 7f on good ground with a win and two places from six similar-going starts, her hold-up style needs something to aim at off Velvet Rhythm's steady lead, and 14 days since last run is a routine gap for this yard.
runners_data.comment: Donna Nook won two starts back before finishing fourth last time, with form at today's trip and ground in the book. A first-time tongue-tie and visor plus a quick 14-day turnaround could sharpen her for this, though she has yet to build on that victory.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Queen
runners_data.note: Tindall's 5lb claim is the headline angle here, though recent form of 8th and 9th at this exact trip and going combination is a concern; a hold-up operator who has not converted on similar ground in 15 attempts without a win or place.
runners_data.comment: Ziggy's Queen tops these figures, improving with each of her last three starts to finish fifth last time. She has won before in this spell and has today's trip and ground covered, with a first-time hood and tongue-tie added; recent inconsistency remains the query.

runners_data.name: Rogue Citation
runners_data.note: 84-day absence is the primary flag for this 3yo, but she won on her second start and has placed at this trip on good ground; P J McDonald compensates for the layoff, and her prominent style means she can get into the race organically without needing Velvet Rhythm to tire.
runners_data.comment: Rogue Citation won two starts back and has today's trip and ground covered, but only managed sixth last time, 84 days ago. She returns fresh and has shown ability, though the long lay-off and that below-par run leave a query.

runners_data.name: Velvet Rhythm
runners_data.note: Three wins from five runs on similar ground, including back-to-back 7f victories; Charlie Johnston's operation is in fair nick and Rowan Scott is familiar with the horse — the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that she is racing from a position that requires her to do the work, which she has repeatedly done well.
runners_data.comment: Velvet Rhythm has three wins from her last five starts, following a dip to fourth and eighth with a fresh success last time. She has today's trip and ground covered and returns quickly, though that in-and-out record leaves a slight question mark.

runners_data.name: Lady Gormire
runners_data.note: Genuine placed form on good ground at shorter trips and a tidy record of 0W2P in similar conditions; her natural style is prominent but the density of this field means she is likely ridden closer to midfield, which is slightly against the grain of her best efforts — Sean Kirrane will need to read the unfolding pace carefully.
runners_data.comment: Lady Gormire is without a win in her last four starts but has been frequently placed, including third last time out, and has experience of today's trip. She sits bottom of these figures on ability, though her consistency should keep her involved in the finish.

runners_data.name: Only Dream Big
runners_data.note: Two wins in her last five on good ground, including a 7f victory, underline her ability at this trip; she is a natural hold-up type whose redistribution to midfield in the map reflects that the rear-rank positions are saturated — David Allan must judge whether to commit early or trust a late run off a likely steady pace.
runners_data.comment: Only Dream Big has won her last two starts, has today's trip and ground covered, and adds first-time blinkers today. That recent upturn is hard to ignore, though a modest speed figure leaves her with more to prove against this field.

races.paceDynamic: Velvet Rhythm is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge her, she is set to control this 7f contest at Catterick on good-to-firm ground without meaningful pressure. Lady Gormire is a natural prominent racer but, with Velvet Rhythm already occupying that role and the field too competitive for multiple horses to dictate, Lady Gormire is unlikely to secure her preferred position and will be shuffled into midfield. The field contains more pace and prominent intent than the race shape can accommodate — Lady Gormire and Only Dream Big are both horses whose natural style is compressed by the structure, meaning the map overstates their positional comfort. With a single uncontested leader setting a sustainable tempo on a track that inherently favours those who travel prominently, this race shape strongly favours horses that can either sit close to the pace and quicken off it, or at minimum travel in a handy enough position to pounce in the straight — deep hold-up tactics are structurally disadvantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Velvet Rhythm Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Velvet Rhythm leads undisturbed and sets a measured but honest gallop, she converts front-running authority into a winning performance.
scenarios.body: Velvet Rhythm has won three of her last five on similar ground and carries the tactical advantage of dictating throughout; with no rival willing or able to apply sustained early pressure, she can conserve energy and pick up again in the Catterick straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Velvet Rhythm sets a pace that proves just quick enough to tire her inside the final furlong, a horse travelling close to her can pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Rogue Citation has the style and the form reference of a close-up finisher, and Lady Gormire's good-ground placed form at shorter trips suggests she could track and challenge if the pace lifts early enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong and the field strings out, a horse held up off the pace could exploit tired rivals late.
scenarios.body: Donna Nook showed a placed effort at 7f on good ground in her history and Tudhope's tactical nous could position her to benefit; Only Dream Big has winning form at this trip but her redistribution away from her natural hold-up position makes her execution less reliable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Flood
scenarios.trigger: If Velvet Rhythm goes too slow early, bunches the field and creates a sprint finish, hold-up types could theoretically finish strongly.
scenarios.body: However, both Donna Nook and Only Dream Big are either out of true position or lack the class advantage to overhaul rivals in a cavalry charge; Ziggy's Queen's recent form figures of 8-9 make this the least reliable shape for the field.

watchPoints.text: Velvet Rhythm's uncontested lead is the race-shaping fact — if she goes untroubled from stall to straight, watch whether any rival has both the position and the energy to close her down inside the final furlong.
Lady Gormire's inability to secure her natural prominent berth is a live tactical hazard; if she gets squeezed back behind the pace early, her chance may be compromised before the race truly begins.
Rogue Citation returns from an 84-day absence — watch the market move and early paddock reports, as a forward show would significantly upgrade her probability of landing scenario B.

Only Dream Big and Donna Nook both carry redistribution or positional baggage; if either is seen travelling kindly in mid-division at the 3f mark, that is the signal that a late run is forming behind the leader.

The going report confirms Good To Firm at 7f throughout the card — any late watering or track staff reports of changing conditions could alter the surface advantage, particularly for horses flagged with going concerns.
